body: #11560 would need to change back to iterating the list though.
Not returning the same object each time from a getter seems very surprising. Why would we want that? You don't want `obj.x !== obj.x` (there's a rule for this in the design principles as well).

Step 1 says to return a an empty `DOMStringList` if this's relevant Document is null.

Since the relevant Document can change over time, I think we can't return the same object always. So options are:

1. Cache whatever was returned the first time the getter is called. (This matches WebKit.)
2. Return a new object every time. (Gecko, Chromium.)
3. Maybe throw an `InvalidStateError` in step 1?

The current spec is wrong since it says `SameObject` but then in step 1 sometimes returns an empty list (not a `DOMStringList`).

We don't have to return the same object always to not violate `obj.x !== obj.x`. Caching or throwing would work. Caching is probably the most compatible. `SameObject` is indeed wrong if the returned value has to change at certain points in time though.

Can you observe the object changing in WebKit? Maybe with initial `about:blank`?

Yes, for example removing an `iframe`. But since WebKit caches the return value from the first access, it's different if you call the getter first before or after the `iframe` is removed.

https://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/saved/14480

Maybe option 4 is to create an empty `DOMStringList` in step 1 but cache it, so there can be two separate objects returned.

I think if you navigate an `iframe` its `Location` object stays the same, but the relevant `Document` changes as well. (Even across a cross-origin navigation I'm pretty sure as you're holding a proxy object, essentially.) We probably want to invalidate the list each time the relevant `Document` changes. Not a 100% sure how to best specify this though.

This PR computes a new list when a `Document` is created and stores it on the `Document` object, so that is solved by this PR.

About the chaching or throwing issue, should we go with option 4?
@theIDinside it's ok to have a new object when there's a semantic change, but just accessing `ancestorOrigins` twice *without* removing an iframe or navigating should give the same object both times.
OK I've attempted to fix this in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12071/commits/e3091d3d9239fac6f309195d567060a6add8dc90
https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/56635 updated also.

This feels unsafe because this would allow you to smuggle state across the origin boundary potentially. We don't really want to create new `Location` associated objects as they have to be their own proxies and such.

> This feels unsafe because this would allow you to smuggle state across the origin boundary potentially. We don't really want to create new `Location` associated objects as they have to be their own proxies and such.

The `DOMStringList` I don't think would be associated with the location object though? It's just POD that's been generated at access time with [NewObject], or what am I missing?

[NewObject] here would be wrong as it results in `obj.field !== obj.field` which we don't want. But the PR is not proposing that. The PR does however have this: ```

A Location object has an associated empty DOMStringList which is a DOMStringList object whose associated list is an empty list.

``` Which I'm pretty sure is wrong (we had to remove `URLSearchParams` for `Location` because of this).

Right. Do we have other spec language to describe this sort of "same object, but not really same object" that `Location` forces us into that we can re-use maybe?

Because it seems like Location in the "normal" use case, has a document, and therefore a DOMStringList it'll "always" produce for that state, and all other scenarios are "in an invalid state"-scenarios (ish. relevant document is null).

Must the empty list have object identity? Because that has meaning. It would be saying that the Location has not changed state since the last time you read an ancestorOrigins list. But if we're allowed to return non-same-objects for the empty case, maybe that would make this easier to spec?

I think if we change the object each time the associated document changes we're okay. Maybe a `Location` object cannot go from a null associated document to a non-null associated document? In that case the current solution might not be observably different from what I want, but it makes me a little uneasy.
@annevk how about returning a new object every time only when "relevant Document" is null?
We don't want to change the semantics of getters so drastically I think. We ought to know when the associated document changes. We'll just have to make sure it all adds up I think.
I couldn't figure out a case where the relevant Document changes from null to non-null. Is it possible?

> I couldn't figure out a case where the relevant Document changes from null to non-null. Is it possible?

No it is not.

We should probably explain in a comment or some such about why this works then as it's not entirely obvious and it's a bit of a hack.

(If we had a proper algorithmic flow here we'd be creating the object whenever we set the `Location` object's associated document to a new value.)
Note added in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12071/commits/a9319d48e85e481434c6e0f8b44b5b1c2d30abe4
